tone.note: "Seattle Freeze": locals are described as "very polite but not particularly friendly" to strangers — keep local NPC lines courteous, brief, low-key; few unprompted chats.
Washington ranked 48th of 50 states for extraversion (2008 study cited by Wikipedia) — locals default to nods, "sorry", "you're good".

Honking is rare and seen as rude: ~3 in 4 Northwest drivers said they rarely or never honk (PEMCO 2017); attitudes softened by 2021 (65% say honking at least somewhat appropriate). NPC reaction to player honking near spots: surprised/disapproving, not aggressive.
Coffee culture: Seattle drinks more coffee than any other US city; espresso small talk is a safe icebreaker.
Rain talk is universal small talk; locals rarely use umbrellas (hoods/rain shells) — common local self-image, unsourced folklore: keep light.

Visitors: Canada was 73% of Seattle's 2.4 M international visitors in 2024; then China, India, UK, South Korea, Germany, Japan, Australia, France, Taiwan — languages used: English, French (Québec), Mandarin, Hindi, Korean, German, Japanese, Spanish (domestic + Latin America).
Indigenous art (totems, Salish Welcome): staff/guides speak respectfully; no jokes about sacred objects.
Guardrails: no stereotypes, accents written phonetically, slurs, politics or alcohol jokes about any group; tourists are curious and happy, locals helpful-but-reserved.

plaques.title: Since 1907
plaques.text: Pike Place Market opened on August 17, 1907, and is one of the oldest continuously operated public farmers' markets in the United States.

plaques.title: The sign
plaques.text: The Public Market Center clock and sign went up on a new 1937 roof; designed by architect Andrew Willatsen, it was one of the largest neon signs on the West Coast.

plaques.title: Rachel
plaques.text: Rachel, a 550 lb bronze piggy bank by Georgia Gerber, was dedicated on the market's 79th birthday in 1986; donations fund the Market's social services.

plaques.title: Flying fish
plaques.text: Pike Place Fish Market (founded 1930) nearly went bankrupt in 1986, then became "world famous" by throwing fish; up to 10,000 people watch on a summer day.

plaques.title: The Gum Wall
plaques.text: Gum started appearing here in the 1990s while theatre-goers waited in line; as of 2024 the wall is 54 ft long and 8 ft high, about 180 pieces of gum per brick.

plaques.title: Original Starbucks
plaques.text: Starbucks opened in 1971 at 2000 Western Ave and moved to 1912 Pike Place in 1977, where it still uses the original siren logo.

structures.name: The Troll (1990; Steve Badanes, Will Martin, Donna Walter, Ross Whitehead)
structures.form: Only the head, shoulders and two huge hands emerge from the ground, as if rising out of the earth under the bridge: long shaggy hair and beard flowing down the torso, big bulbous nose, heavy brow; the visible (its left, viewer-right) eye is a shiny VW hubcap, the other eye is hidden under hair. Its right hand (viewer-left) is splayed flat on the ground with long knobbly fingers; its left hand (viewer-right) clamps a real Volkswagen Beetle (California plate) that is cast over / painted the same grey so it reads as a rounded lump under the fingers. Rough sculpted ferro-cement with blue-grey paint patches, chalk/graffiti traces cleaned by volunteers. Big boulders around the base; new concrete stairs (rebuilt Sept 2023) climb on the viewer-right side up to the shoulder/head; visitors sit on the hand and nose.

plaques.title: Underground Seattle
plaques.text: After the Great Fire of June 6, 1889, streets were raised by up to a storey, leaving old sidewalks and storefronts below — the Seattle Underground.

plaques.title: Purple glass

plaques.title: The totem pole

spots.name: Bellevue Downtown Park
spots.blurb: A 20-acre circle of lawn ringed by a half-mile promenade and a stepped canal ending in a 240-ft-wide waterfall, with the Bellevue skyline rising behind.
spots.why_top10: Wikivoyage Bellevue "Downtown Park" (cascading waterfall in a circular loop); PlanetWare #1 attraction in Bellevue; Visit Bellevue listing; city flagship park.

extent.vertical: Mostly flat; waterfall drop ~3 m into the pond (estimate).
